Sive Speelman

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
From a "ski pup" to an Olympian - we bring you the story of Sive Speelman.

Unique Selling Point:
Skiing is not the sport of choice in South Africa for obvious reasons, but for Sive Speelman, it was an option as he grew up in rural eastern cape near South Africa’s only ski resort at Tiffendell, near the Drakensburg Mountains.
Sive was in a Carte Blanche story on the resort back in 2008, and is now on the Winter Olympic team for 2018 in Pyeongchang, South Korea. He is the first black skier from South Africa. He qualified in 2014 for Sochi but was bitterly disappointed when SASCOC decided not to send him for monetary reasons.
He is again on the team and has qualified and again, they may not send him, even though they have put a lot of money into developing him as a talent, and have sent him around the world.


Summary:
He has competed in international competitions and come within the top 20. The Olympics is his dream, and was something, he and his teammate Tsotane Dywili spoke about in the previous story. This story is an inspirational tale of how a lad, who started out as a “ski pup” in a program at Tiffendell ski resort has made it all the way to competing against the best. Even meeting his idol Bode Miller- America and Olympic Champion.
After he was not taken to the previous Olympic Sive was heartbroken and his life took a turn for the worst. He became involved in illicit activities, and it was up to his coach Alex Heath and his father John Speelman to bring him back from the brink.


Further information:
He is now back, and better than ever, having overcome some of the troubles youths in rural areas and townships encounter. He is an inspiration to his small town, and to the many children who surround him. He has also been sponsored by Tiffendel and Snow Sports – two organizations working together to develop talent in the surrounding areas and allow children to learn about the sport.
This is a feelgood story, that will hopefully have a happy ending. SASCOC say they will decide on the 22nd of this month.

Press Release:


SA Skier Qualifies For Olympics
Barkly East at the foot of the Maluti mountains in the Eastern Cape, is about as far as you can get from the famous ski resorts of the world and these slopes only have snow for 3 months of the year. Yet from this small town, a young man has emerged who has actually qualified for the winter Olympics next month in South Korea. Carte Blanche goes skiing with 22-year-old Sive Speelman.


Script:


SKIING SHOTS
Ski pups
Maluti mountains Skiing - the playground of the rich and famous – where South Africa is not the first country that comes to mind - But Tiffendel – at nearly 3,000m is our highest resort, nestled in the Mountains of the Eastern Cape - has been challenging that perception. This has given birth to the Ski Pups program – which nurtures young athletes, teaching them the sport.
See sive skiing… Sive: “Up there when you’re in the nature, doing what you love, it’s just the best feeling ever.”
Old story
In 2008 Carte Blanche took to these slopes and met ski pups Tsostane “Tsotsi” Dywili and Sive speelman. Tsosti grew up nearby….While Sive lives 80km away in Barkly East. Coach Alex Heath, who was also a three time Olympian, had big plans for them.
Derek + Alex Derek: “Are you satisfied with their performance?”
Alex: “I’m happy with the way they are progressing.”
Sive intv Derek: “Sive, you were 12/13 when I last saw you, you were a pretty chubby teen, and now you’re long and lean.”
Sive: “yeah I was still young back then.”
Derek: “So from the age of 9 you’ve been dreaming about the Olympics.”
Sive: “In the beginning it felt like a long shot. Ever since then, its been one of my biggest dreams…”
Tsotsi Now, Sive is 22 and Tsotsi is 25 AND both have qualified for next month’s winter Olympics in Pyeongchang, South Korea. But only one person from South Africa can actually go.
Sive intv Sive: “He started the year before me, and he was the best, before I started beating him. But that never changed our friendship.”
Tsotsi intv Tsotsi: “Alex messaged me on facebook, and said dude, did you know that you qualified, and then I was so proud and very very happy.”
Sive intv Derek: “Since then you’re taken over the national championships and you’ve won, just about every year?
Sive: “Thanks to my friends, cos they’re the ones who pushed me, cos I don’t really like losing.”
Intro to SASCOC Although Sive is the fastest qualifier in the slalom event, it’s the South African Sports Confederation and Olympic Committee – known as SASCOC – who will decide whether or not South Africa will even participate in the Winter Olympics.
DEREK LINK LINK: “AT JUST 18 SIVE WAS GEARED FOR THE BIGGEST MOMENT OF HIS LIFE, AND ABOUT TO MAKE HISTORY…”
Sochi Russia He qualified for the 2014 winter Olympics in Sochi, Russia – the moment he found out was captured on camera.
Sive video of him qualifying - 2014 Video: “ (big smile)I’m very happy, its my dream.”
DEREK LINK LINK: “…AND THEN HE GOT THE BAD NEWS, HE WOULDN’T BE GOING TO THE WINTER OLYMPICS IN RUSSIA, A DECISION MADE BY HIS OWN GAMES COMMITTEE.”
SASCOC SASCOC decided to not send a team to represent South Africa.
Tsotsane intv Tsotsi: “Apparently, we don’t meet the requirements to go, cos we’re not going to win a medal, I don’t really understand it, cos it’s not about winning, its about competing to be there.”
Sive intv Sive: I was just shattered. You know all the hard work, all the years, sacrifice, and not just being sent.”
Derek: “But, it was such a bad knock?”
Sive: “Yeah I’ll never forget it in my life it left a scar.”
Old story John John speelman, who visited the slopes for the first time with us 10 years ago, says his son was devastated.
John intv John Speelman: “He was heartbroken. He didn’t want to show me, but he told me afterwards and I saw how much it meant to him.”
Intro ref His teamate – Refeletso Thipa – says they all felt his pain.
Refeletso Ref: “We had to pick him up, cos we were also hurt cos cos we train together, and he was the one that made it to the Olympics.”
Intv sice Derek: “How were the next few weeks and months?”
Sive: “Through friends and family, alex and supporting me and pushing me, just to prove to the people that I could do it again, kinda got me thinking, yeah why not. I’m going to come back better and came back a better person, a better athlete.”
St. Morritz world championships Which he proved when he made the finals at the World Championships in 2017 in St. Moritz Switzerland.
Intv sive Sive: “It’s very steep and icy, and you start thinking man ive got to go down this, and you’re the start gate… Its very tough, being there, representing, and especially making it in the finals for slalom that was really great.”
Derek: “And the other competitors, when you say you’re from South Africa.?”
Sive: “Even walking in town, cos you’re black … im a skier.”
Intro to Peter Pilz Accompanying the South African Athletes is the winter sports federation - Snow Sports South Africa - Director Peter Pilz. He recognized Tsostane and Sive’s talent back when the ski pups were formed.
Peter intv Peter: “I was just so impressed with their character, their enthusiasm, and how much they fell in love with the sport.”
LINK DEREK: “THE SKI PUPS HAS GROWN TO MORE THAN 50 KIDS, AND THE OLDEST SKIERS ATTEND THE ACADEMY IN THE WINTER, TRAINING IN THE MORNING, AND KEEPING UP WITH SCHOOL WORK IN THE AFTERNOON.”
Alex intv Alex: “You have 130-140 athletes at the Olympics, only three will make medals, so you have to ask yourself what is the point? The Olympics brings everyone together.”
Peter intv Peter: “So many of the top level athletes, when you ask them what they remember they say in your career, they say what do you remember, the medals are wonderful, but the friendship…etc”
UPSOUND SOUNDUP: “Welcome to Sunny South Africa 2016 skichampionships….the first black snowman…”
Tsotsi intro Tsoti is now based at Tiffendell’s Ferndale head office in Johannesburg.
Tsotsi Tsotsi: “I’m a ski instructor, a lot of people ask me what is that? There’s not an exact word for skiing in Xhlosa so we just call it skiing.”
Shows ski Helping the athletes prepare for competition, this machine assists them to train, by following a simulation of a ski-course.
DEREK LINK DEREK: “WITH ONLY 3 MONTHS OF SNOW A YEAR AT TIFFENDELL, SIVE HAS TO TRY AND MAINTAIN HIS FITNESS WITH STRENGTH AND FLEXABILITY EXERCISES, HERE ON THE DUSTY FIELDS OF HIS OLD HIGHSCHOOL IN BARKLY EAST.”
Sive intv Derek: “The guys you’re up against, a lot of them just live amongst the snow, how can you compete at that level?”
Sive: “It takes every second in snow, so you’ve got to wake up in the morning, get on the slopes, even before you coach.”
Tsotsi Tsotsi: “It’s actually difficult for us to adapt in Europe because we don’t get time to train, so we arrive and train for two days beforehand, so it’s tough.”
Shots of his family During the Summer, when Sive’s home with his family and not on the slopes, he’s still thinking of the snow.
John intv Derek: “You must be very proud.”
John: “Yes, I was.”
Derek: “You’ve never seen him compete oversees, but you’ve seen him on TV?”
John Speelman: “it’s the first time any of our family members were on tv, for everyone to see him ski.”
Sive intv
MUST SAY: “Hello bhut’ Sive” Derek: when you walk through barkly east?
Sive: “Yes even little kids just shout out…Hello brother!”
Sive says once he’s finished with his career he wants to join Totsi and train the ski pups to continue what Alex and Peter started.
Sive intv Sive: “My main dream, is to see somebody else like me, making it to the Olympics and I know that I helped, and that is my main goal. 9:00
